query: Reported superconducting high-entropy alloys are dominated by Nb-Ta matrices, while other studies concern titanium-rich systems based on heavy transition metals and partly ordered systems. Consequently, these precedents do not establish what controls superconductivity in high-entropy alloys outside the best-studied material classes. Within the defining constraint of a solid solution containing at least five elements at no less than 5 atomic percent each, what governs superconducting behavior in such an uncharacterized high-entropy alloy, and why? State one testable mechanistic hypothesis, a controlled comparison against the starting material, predicted observations relative to the baseline, applicable boundary conditions, the earlier evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In equimolar five‐element Hf–Nb–Ti–V–Zr high‐entropy alloys, the superconducting critical temperature (Tc) is governed primarily by the average valence electron concentration (VEC) per atom. Raising the average VEC increases the electronic density of states at the Fermi level, which enhances the electron–phonon coupling constant (λ) and thus raises Tc.
generation.material_initial_state: Polycrystalline equiatomic HfNbTiVZr solid solution (each element 20 at. %, average VEC ≈4.40, Tc≈0.5 K).
generation.intervention: Partial substitution of 5 at.% Zr (VEC=4) by Nb (VEC=5), yielding Hf20–Nb25–Ti20–V20–Zr15 at.% (average VEC ≈4.45).
generation.conditions: Synthesis by arc melting and annealing at 1200 °C under argon, measurement from 0.3 K to 4 K in a PPMS under zero applied magnetic field.
generation.structural_mediator: Average valence electron concentration per atom.
generation.mechanism: Increasing VEC raises the electronic density of states at the Fermi level, enhancing electron–phonon coupling (λ∝N(0)), which elevates Tc.
generation.predicted_outcome: Tc of the Nb‐enriched alloy will increase by ~0.1–0.3 K above the 0.5 K baseline, with a corresponding larger heat‐capacity jump ΔC at Tc.
generation.boundary: Valid for single‐phase, equimolar (±5 at. %) five‐element solid solutions with average VEC between ~4.0 and 4.8; not expected to hold if partial ordering or secondary phases form or if VEC exceeds ~5.0.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate; the exact Tc shift depends on concomitant changes in phonon spectra and disorder scattering.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize (a) baseline Hf20–Nb20–Ti20–V20–Zr20 at.% and (b) Nb‐enriched Hf20–Nb25–Ti20–V20–Zr15 at.% by identical arc‐melting and annealing procedures. Measure electrical resistivity, magnetic susceptibility, and heat capacity from 0.3 K to 4 K under zero field.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the substituted alloy shows no Tc increase (ΔTc≤0 K within ±0.05 K) or a decrease in Tc relative to baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
